sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śamo bahuvidhākāraḥ sūkṣma uktaḥ pitāmaha na ca me hṛdaye śāntir asti kṛtvedam īdṛśam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tranquillity, grandfather, you have called manifold in form and subtle; yet there is no peace in my heart, having done such a deed as this.

sanskrit: asminn arthe bahuvidhā śāntir uktā tvayānagha svakṛte kā nu śāntiḥ syāc chamād bahuvidhād api
english: On this matter, O sinless one, you have spoken of peace in its many kinds; but for one's own deed, what peace could there be, even through tranquillity of every manifold sort?

sanskrit: śarācitaśarīraṃ hi tīvravraṇam udīkṣya ca śamaṃ nopalabhe vīra duṣkṛtāny eva cintayan
english: Beholding your body studded with arrows and its grievous wounds, O hero, I find no peace, brooding only upon my evil deeds.

sanskrit: rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgaṃ prasravantaṃ yathācalam tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghra sīde varṣāsv ivāmbujam
english: Seeing you, O tiger among men, your limbs drenched in blood and streaming like a mountain, I wither as a lotus withers in the rains.

sanskrit: ataḥ kaṣṭataraṃ kiṃ nu matkṛte yat pitāmahaḥ imām avasthāṃ gamitaḥ pratyamitrai raṇājire tathaivānye nṛpatayaḥ sahaputrāḥ sabāndhavāḥ
english: What can be more grievous than this — that on my account the grandfather has been brought by his foes to such a state on the field of battle, and likewise other kings, together with their sons and kinsmen?

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca kālamanyuvaśānugāḥ kṛtvedaṃ ninditaṃ karma prāpsyāmaḥ kāṃ gatiṃ nṛpa
english: For we and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra alike, in thrall to time and to wrath, having wrought this blameworthy deed — what destiny shall we attain, O king?

sanskrit: ahaṃ tava hy antakaraḥ suhṛdvadhakaras tathā na śāntim adhigacchāmi paśyaṃs tvāṃ duḥkhitaṃ kṣitau
english: I am the cause of your end and the slayer of my own kinsmen; I can find no peace, beholding you stricken upon the ground.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca paratantraṃ kathaṃ hetum ātmānam anupaśyasi karmaṇy asmin mahābhāga sūkṣmaṃ hy etad atīndriyam
english: Bhīṣma said: How do you regard yourself, who are subject to another's will, as the cause in this deed, O greatly fortunate one? Subtle indeed is this matter, and beyond the senses.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam saṃvādaṃ mṛtyugautamyoḥ kālalubdhakapannagaiḥ
english: On this they recite this ancient tale — the colloquy between Death and Gautamī, together with Time, the fowler, and the serpent.

sanskrit: gautamī nāma kaunteya sthavirā śamasaṃyutā sarpeṇa daṣṭaṃ svaṃ putram apaśyad gatacetanam
english: An aged woman named Gautamī, O son of Kuntī, endowed with tranquillity, beheld her own son, bitten by a serpent, lying senseless.

sanskrit: atha taṃ snāyupāśena baddhvā sarpam amarṣitaḥ lubdhako 'rjunako nāma gautamyāḥ samupānayat
english: Then a fowler named Arjunaka, full of indignation, bound that serpent with a sinew-snare and brought it before Gautamī.

sanskrit: tāṃ cābravīd ayaṃ te sa putrahā pannagādhamaḥ brūhi kṣipraṃ mahābhāge vadhyatāṃ kena hetunā
english: And he said to her: This vile serpent is the slayer of your son. Tell me quickly, O greatly fortunate one, by what means it shall be put to death.

sanskrit: agnau prakṣipyatām eṣa cchidyatāṃ khaṇḍaśo 'pi vā na hy ayaṃ bālahā pāpaś ciraṃ jīvitum arhati
english: Let it be cast into the fire, or else be cut to pieces; for this wicked killer of a child does not deserve to live long.

sanskrit: gautamy uvāca visṛjainam abuddhis tvaṃ na vadhyo 'rjunaka tvayā ko hy ātmānaṃ guruṃ kuryāt prāptavye sati cintayan
english: Gautamī said: Release it, Arjunaka; you are without understanding. It is not for you to slay it. Who, reflecting on what is yet to be attained, would burden his own soul with such a grievous weight?

sanskrit: plavante dharmalaghavo loke 'mbhasi yathā plavāḥ majjanti pāpaguravaḥ śastraṃ skannam ivodake
english: Those made light by righteousness float in the world, as rafts float upon the water; but those made heavy by sin sink, as a weapon dropped into water.

sanskrit: na cāmṛtyur bhavitā vai hate 'smin; ko vātyayaḥ syād ahate 'smiñ janasya asyotsarge prāṇayuktasya jantor; mṛtyor lokaṃ ko nu gacched anantam
english: Nor will my son be freed from death by the slaying of this creature; and what harm would befall the people were it left unslain? By the destroying of this living, breathing thing, who could pass into the endless realm of Death?

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca jānāmy evaṃ neha guṇāguṇajñāḥ; sarve niyuktā guravo vai bhavanti svasthasyaite tūpadeśā bhavanti; tasmāt kṣudraṃ sarpam enaṃ haniṣye
english: The fowler said: I know that here in this world not all who are enjoined to such tasks discern merit from demerit; the elders are reverend indeed. But these counsels are for one at ease; therefore I shall slay this base serpent.

sanskrit: samīpsantaḥ kālayogaṃ tyajanti; sadyaḥ śucaṃ tv arthavidas tyajanti śreyaḥ kṣayaḥ śocatāṃ nityaśo hi; tasmāt tyājyaṃ jahi śokaṃ hate 'smin
english: Those who seek their end await the working of time; but the wise, who know the truth, cast off grief at once. Constant sorrowing brings only decay of one's good; therefore grief is to be abandoned. Cast off your sorrow when this creature is slain.

sanskrit: gautamy uvāca na caivārtir vidyate 'smadvidhānāṃ; dharmārāmaḥ satataṃ sajjano hi nityāyasto bālajano na cāsti; dharmo hy eṣa prabhavāmy asya nāham
english: Gautamī said: No such anguish is found in such as we, for the virtuous ever take their delight in righteousness. The childish, by contrast, are forever vexed; but this is righteousness, and I have no power over this serpent's life.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇānāṃ kopo 'sti kutaḥ kopāc ca yātanā mārdavāt kṣamyatāṃ sādho mucyatām eṣa pannagaḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas know no wrath; and whence, then, should torment proceed from wrath? Out of gentleness let it be forgiven, O good man; let this serpent go free.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca hatvā lābhaḥ śreya evāvyayaṃ syāt; sadyo lābho balavadbhiḥ praśastaḥ kālāl lābho yas tu sadyo bhaveta; hate śreyaḥ kutsite tvīdṛśe syāt
english: The fowler said: From the slaying a gain would come, an imperishable good; an immediate gain is praised by the mighty. The gain that springs at once is better than one drawn out in time; and in slaying so contemptible a thing, there is surely benefit.

sanskrit: gautamy uvāca kārthaprāptir gṛhya śatruṃ nihatya; kā vā śāntiḥ prāpya śatruṃ namuktvā kasmāt saumya bhujage na kṣameyaṃ; mokṣaṃ vā kiṃ kāraṇaṃ nāsya kuryām
english: Gautamī said: What end is gained by seizing and slaying an enemy? And what peace, by holding a captured foe and not releasing him? Why, gentle one, should I not forgive the serpent? For what reason should I not grant it release?

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca asmād ekasmād bahavo rakṣitavyā; naiko bahubhyo gautami rakṣitavyaḥ kṛtāgasaṃ dharmavidas tyajanti; sarīsṛpaṃ pāpam imaṃ jahi tvam
english: The fowler said: From this single creature the many must be protected; one is not to be protected at the cost of many, Gautamī. Those who know righteousness abandon the offender; so slay this wicked, crawling thing.

sanskrit: gautamy uvāca nāsmin hate pannage putrako me; saṃprāpsyate lubdhaka jīvitaṃ vai guṇaṃ cānyaṃ nāsya vadhe prapaśye; tasmāt sarpaṃ lubdhaka muñca jīvam
english: Gautamī said: By the slaying of this serpent my little son will not regain his life, O fowler; nor do I see any other good in its killing. Therefore, fowler, set the serpent free, alive.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca vṛtraṃ hatvā devarāṭ śreṣṭhabhāg vai; yajñaṃ hatvā bhāgam avāpa caiva śūlī devo devavṛttaṃ kuru tvaṃ; kṣipraṃ sarpaṃ jahi mā bhūd viśaṅkā
english: The fowler said: By slaying Vṛtra the king of the gods won the foremost portion; and the trident-bearing god, by destroying the sacrifice, gained his share. Act, then, as the gods act: slay the serpent at once, and let there be no hesitation.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca asakṛt procyamānāpi gautamī bhujagaṃ prati lubdhakena mahābhāgā pāpe naivākaron matim
english: Bhīṣma said: Though urged again and again by the fowler concerning the serpent, the greatly fortunate Gautamī set not her mind upon the sinful deed.

sanskrit: īṣad ucchvasamānas tu kṛcchrāt saṃstabhya pannagaḥ utsasarja giraṃ mandāṃ mānuṣīṃ pāśapīḍitaḥ
english: Then the serpent, breathing faintly and with difficulty steadying itself, oppressed by its bonds, uttered slow words in a human voice.

sanskrit: ko nv arjunaka doṣo 'tra vidyate mama bāliśa asvatantraṃ hi māṃ mṛtyur vivaśaṃ yad acūcudat
english: What fault is there in me here, foolish Arjunaka? For it was Death who, having me powerless and not my own master, drove me to it.

sanskrit: tasyāyaṃ vacanād daṣṭo na kopena na kāmyayā tasya tat kilbiṣaṃ lubdha vidyate yadi kilbiṣam
english: It was at his bidding that this child was bitten, not out of my own wrath nor out of desire; if any guilt there be, O fowler, that guilt is his.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca yady anyavaśagenedaṃ kṛtaṃ te pannagāśubham kāraṇaṃ vai tvam apy atra tasmāt tvam api kilbiṣī
english: The fowler said: If this evil deed of yours was done while subject to another, O serpent, still you too are a cause in it; therefore you too bear the guilt.

sanskrit: mṛtpātrasya kriyāyāṃ hi daṇḍacakrādayo yathā kāraṇatve prakalpyante tathā tvam api pannaga
english: For in the making of an earthen pot, just as the rod and the wheel and the rest are reckoned among the causes, so too are you, O serpent.

sanskrit: kilbiṣī cāpi me vadhyaḥ kilbiṣī cāsi pannaga ātmānaṃ kāraṇaṃ hy atra tvam ākhyāsi bhujaṃgama
english: The guilty one is to be slain by me, and guilty you are, O serpent; for you yourself, O snake, declare yourself a cause in this.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca sarva ete hy asvavaśā daṇḍacakrādayo yathā tathāham api tasmān me naiṣa hetur matas tava
english: The serpent said: All these — the rod, the wheel, and the rest — are not their own masters; and so am I. Therefore this is no fault of mine, as you suppose.

sanskrit: atha vā matam etat te te 'py anyonyaprayojakāḥ kāryakāraṇasaṃdeho bhavaty anyonyacodanāt
english: Or if this be your view — that these too are mutually each other's instigators — then a doubt about effect and cause arises from their mutual impelling.

sanskrit: evaṃ sati na doṣo me nāsmi vadhyo na kilbiṣī kilbiṣaṃ samavāye syān manyase yadi kilbiṣam
english: This being so, there is no fault in me; I am neither to be slain nor guilty. The guilt, if you reckon there to be guilt, would lie in the concurrence of them all.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca kāraṇaṃ yadi na syād vai na kartā syās tvam apy uta vināśe kāraṇaṃ tvaṃ ca tasmād vadhyo 'si me mataḥ
english: The fowler said: If you were not a cause, then you would not be a doer either; but you are indeed a cause in this destruction, and therefore I hold that you are to be slain.

sanskrit: asaty api kṛte kārye neha pannaga lipyate tasmān nātraiva hetuḥ syād vadhyaḥ kiṃ bahu bhāṣase
english: Even when the effect is not yet wrought, the cause is not thereby tainted here, O serpent; yet you are to be slain — why speak so much?

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca kāryābhāve kriyā na syāt saty asaty api kāraṇe tasmāt tvam asmin hetau me vācyo hetur viśeṣataḥ
english: The serpent said: When there is no effect, there can be no action, whether the cause be present or absent. Therefore, of the causes in this matter, you above all are to be charged as the cause.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ kāraṇatvena mato lubdhaka tattvataḥ anyaḥ prayoge syād atra kilbiṣī jantunāśane
english: If, in truth, I am held to be a cause, O fowler, then another is the agent who applied it, and his is the guilt in the slaying of this living thing.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca vadhyas tvaṃ mama durbuddhe bālaghātī nṛśaṃsakṛt bhāṣase kiṃ bahu punar vadhyaḥ san pannagādhama
english: The fowler said: You are to be slain by me, O fool, killer of a child and doer of cruelty. Why speak so much, when you are doomed to die, O vile serpent?

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca yathā havīṃṣi juhvānā makhe vai lubdhakartvijaḥ na phalaṃ prāpnuvanty atra paraloke tathā hy aham
english: The serpent said: As officiating priests who, greedy at a sacrifice, pour out the oblations gain no fruit thereby in the world beyond, so it is with me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tathā bruvati tasmiṃs tu pannage mṛtyucodite ājagāma tato mṛtyuḥ pannagaṃ cābravīd idam
english: Bhīṣma said: While the serpent, impelled by Death, was speaking thus, Death himself came forth, and spoke this word to the serpent.

sanskrit: kālenāhaṃ praṇuditaḥ pannaga tvām acūcudam vināśahetur nāsya tvam ahaṃ vā prāṇinaḥ śiśoḥ
english: Impelled by Time, O serpent, I urged you on; neither you nor I am the cause of the destruction of this living child.

sanskrit: yathā vāyur jaladharān vikarṣati tatas tataḥ tadvaj jaladavat sarpa kālasyāhaṃ vaśānugaḥ
english: As the wind drives the rain-clouds hither and thither, so, like a cloud, O serpent, am I obedient to the will of Time.

sanskrit: sāttvikā rājasāś caiva tāmasā ye ca ke cana bhāvāḥ kālātmakāḥ sarve pravartante hi jantuṣu
english: All states of being whatsoever — those of sattva, those of rajas, and those of tamas — have Time for their essence, and arise in living creatures.

sanskrit: jaṅgamāḥ sthāvarāś caiva divi vā yadi vā bhuvi sarve kālātmakāḥ sarpa kālātmakam idaṃ jagat
english: The moving and the unmoving, whether in heaven or upon the earth — all have Time for their essence, O serpent; this whole world has Time for its essence.

sanskrit: pravṛttayaś ca yā loke tathaiva ca nivṛttayaḥ tāsāṃ vikṛtayo yāś ca sarvaṃ kālātmakaṃ smṛtam
english: Whatever activities there are in the world, and likewise the cessations from them, and whatever transformations of these — all is held to have Time for its essence.

sanskrit: ādityaś candramā viṣṇur āpo vāyuḥ śatakratuḥ agniḥ khaṃ pṛthivī mitra oṣadhyo vasavas tathā
english: The sun, the moon, Viṣṇu, the waters, the wind, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, fire, the sky, the earth, Mitra, the healing herbs, and likewise the Vasus —

sanskrit: saritaḥ sāgarāś caiva bhāvābhāvau ca pannaga sarve kālena sṛjyante hriyante ca tathā punaḥ
english: the rivers and the oceans, and being and non-being too, O serpent — all are by Time created, and by Time again drawn away.

sanskrit: evaṃ jñātvā kathaṃ māṃ tvaṃ sadoṣaṃ sarpa manyase atha caivaṃgate doṣo mayi tvam api doṣavān
english: Knowing this, how can you deem me at fault, O serpent? And if, things being so, the fault were mine, then you too would share in the fault.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca nirdoṣaṃ doṣavantaṃ vā na tvā mṛtyo bravīmy aham tvayāhaṃ codita iti bravīmy etāvad eva tu
english: The serpent said: I do not call you faultless or at fault, O Death; I say only this much — that I was impelled by you.

sanskrit: yadi kāle tu doṣo 'sti yadi tatrāpi neṣyate doṣo naiva parīkṣyo me na hy atrādhikṛtā vayam
english: Whether the fault lies in Time, or whether it be held to lie not even there — the fault is not for me to examine, for in this we hold no authority.

sanskrit: nirmokṣas tv asya doṣasya mayā kāryo yathā tathā mṛtyo vidoṣaḥ syām eva yathā tan me prayojanam
english: Yet the absolving of this fault must somehow be wrought by me, O Death, so that I may be free of fault; that is my whole purpose.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarpo 'thārjunakaṃ prāha śrutaṃ te mṛtyubhāṣitam nānāgasaṃ māṃ pāśena saṃtāpayitum arhasi
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the serpent said to Arjunaka: You have heard the words of Death. It is not fitting for you to torment me, the innocent, with your snare.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca mṛtyoḥ śrutaṃ me vacanaṃ tava caiva bhujaṃgama naiva tāvad vidoṣatvaṃ bhavati tvayi pannaga
english: The fowler said: I have heard the word of Death, and yours as well, O serpent; yet this does not establish your freedom from fault, O snake.

sanskrit: mṛtyus tvaṃ caiva hetur hi jantor asya vināśane ubhayaṃ kāraṇaṃ manye na kāraṇam akāraṇam
english: Both Death and you are causes in the destruction of this creature; I deem both to be the cause. A non-cause cannot be the cause.

sanskrit: dhiṅ mṛtyuṃ ca durātmānaṃ krūraṃ duḥkhakaraṃ satām tvāṃ caivāhaṃ vadhiṣyāmi pāpaṃ pāpasya kāraṇam
english: A curse upon Death, that evil-souled, cruel one who brings grief upon the good; and you too I shall slay — the wicked cause of a wicked deed.

sanskrit: mṛtyur uvāca vivaśau kālavaśagāv āvāṃ tad diṣṭakāriṇau nāvāṃ doṣeṇa gantavyau yadi samyak prapaśyasi
english: Death said: Both of us are helpless, subject to the power of Time, doers of what is ordained; we two are not to be charged with the fault, if you see the matter rightly.

sanskrit: lubdhaka uvāca yuvām ubhau kālavaśau yadi vai mṛtyupannagau harṣakrodhau kathaṃ syātām etad icchāmi veditum
english: The fowler said: If you both, Death and serpent, are subject to the power of Time, then how can there be joy and wrath in you? This I wish to understand.

sanskrit: mṛtyur uvāca yāḥ kāś cid iha ceṣṭāḥ syuḥ sarvāḥ kālapracoditāḥ pūrvam evaitad uktaṃ hi mayā lubdhaka kālataḥ
english: Death said: Whatever activities there are in this world are all impelled by Time; this very thing I have already declared to you, O fowler — that it proceeds from Time.

sanskrit: tasmād ubhau kālavaśāv āvāṃ tad diṣṭakāriṇau nāvāṃ doṣeṇa gantavyau tvayā lubdhaka karhi cit
english: Therefore we two are both subject to the power of Time, doers of what is ordained; we are never to be charged by you with the fault, O fowler.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca athopagamya kālas tu tasmin dharmārthasaṃśaye abravīt pannagaṃ mṛtyuṃ lubdham arjunakaṃ ca tam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Time himself drew near, in that doubt concerning righteousness and its meaning, and spoke to the serpent, to Death, and to that fowler Arjunaka.

sanskrit: kāla uvāca naivāhaṃ nāpy ayaṃ mṛtyur nāyaṃ lubdhaka pannagaḥ kilbiṣī jantumaraṇe na vayaṃ hi prayojakāḥ
english: Time said: Neither I, nor this Death, nor this serpent, O fowler, is guilty in the dying of the creature; for we are not the instigators.

sanskrit: akarod yad ayaṃ karma tan no 'rjunaka codakam praṇāśahetur nānyo 'sya vadhyate 'yaṃ svakarmaṇā
english: The deed that this child himself performed — that, Arjunaka, was our impeller. No other was the cause of his ruin; he is slain by his own deed.

sanskrit: yad anena kṛtaṃ karma tenāyaṃ nidhanaṃ gataḥ vināśahetuḥ karmāsya sarve karmavaśā vayam
english: By the deed that he himself wrought he has come to his end; his own deed is the cause of his destruction. We are all subject to the power of deeds.

sanskrit: karmadāyādavāṃl lokaḥ karmasaṃbandhalakṣaṇaḥ karmāṇi codayantīha yathānyonyaṃ tathā vayam
english: The world inherits its deeds; it is marked by the bond of deeds. As deeds impel one another here, so too are we impelled.

sanskrit: yathā mṛtpiṇḍataḥ kartā kurute yad yad icchati evam ātmakṛtaṃ karma mānavaḥ pratipadyate
english: As from a lump of clay the maker fashions whatever he desires, so does a man come to receive the deed that he himself has wrought.

sanskrit: yathā chāyātapau nityaṃ susaṃbaddhau nirantaram tathā karma ca kartā ca saṃbaddhāv ātmakarmabhiḥ
english: As shadow and sunlight are ever closely bound together without interval, so are the deed and the doer bound by the doer's own deeds.

sanskrit: evaṃ nāhaṃ na vai mṛtyur na sarpo na tathā bhavān na ceyaṃ brāhmaṇī vṛddhā śiśur evātra kāraṇam
english: Thus neither I, nor Death, nor the serpent, nor you, nor this aged brāhmaṇa woman — the child alone is the cause here.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā bruvāṇe tu brāhmaṇī gautamī nṛpa svakarmapratyayāṃl lokān matvārjunakam abravīt
english: When Time had spoken thus, O king, the brāhmaṇa woman Gautamī, deeming the worlds to rest upon one's own deeds, said to Arjunaka:

sanskrit: naiva kālo na bhujago na mṛtyur iha kāraṇam svakarmabhir ayaṃ bālaḥ kālena nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: Neither Time, nor the serpent, nor Death is the cause here; by his own deeds, in the course of time, this child has come to his end.

sanskrit: mayā ca tat kṛtaṃ karma yenāyaṃ me mṛtaḥ sutaḥ yātu kālas tathā mṛtyur muñcārjunaka pannagam
english: And I too wrought that deed by which this son of mine has died. Let Time depart, and Death likewise; release the serpent, Arjunaka.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato yathāgataṃ jagmur mṛtyuḥ kālo 'tha pannagaḥ abhūd viroṣo 'rjunako viśokā caiva gautamī
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Death, Time, and the serpent went each the way it had come; Arjunaka was freed of his anger, and Gautamī of her grief.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā śamaṃ gaccha mā bhūś cintāparo nṛpa svakarmapratyayāṃl lokāṃs trīn viddhi manujarṣabha
english: Having heard this, attain tranquillity; be not given over to brooding, O king. Know that the three worlds rest upon one's own deeds, O bull among men.

sanskrit: na tu tvayā kṛtaṃ pārtha nāpi duryodhanena vai kālena tat kṛtaṃ viddhi vihatā yena pārthivāḥ
english: It was not done by you, O Pārtha, nor indeed by Duryodhana; know that it was done by Time, by which the kings were brought down.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā babhūva vigatajvaraḥ yudhiṣṭhiro mahātejāḥ papracchedaṃ ca dharmavit
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard these words, the mighty-splendored Yudhiṣṭhira, knower of righteousness, became freed of his fever and asked this further:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada śrutaṃ me mahad ākhyānam idaṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Grandfather, greatly wise, versed in all the scriptures — I have heard this noble tale, O best of the discerning.

sanskrit: bhūyas tu śrotum icchāmi dharmārthasahitaṃ nṛpa kathyamānaṃ tvayā kiṃ cit tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yet I wish to hear still more, something joined with righteousness and its meaning, told by you, O king; deign to expound it to me.

sanskrit: kena mṛtyur gṛhasthena dharmam āśritya nirjitaḥ ity etat sarvam ācakṣva tattvena mama pārthiva
english: By what householder was Death conquered, through resort to righteousness? Tell me all this truly, O king.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā mṛtyur gṛhasthena dharmam āśritya nirjitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite this ancient tale — how Death was conquered by a householder through resort to righteousness.
